chapter: Jess Stacy, Goodman and New York characters
title: Musicians' brotherhood despite the critics
summary: Hodes says musicians have grown closer despite critics. He wonders whether Feather and Ulanov are still friends.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: The relationship with musicians, as you say, is a brotherhood, with no color, no -- and that remains, in spite of the critics. We have outlived that. They've done their worst and we're still together. I'm not sure that Leonard and Ulanov are buddy-buddy. I would be interested to find out.
I have a feeling that they're not. Barry went off into something -- he was quite intellectual, was teaching at a college in New York. I guess he still is, English literature.

But the musicians have gotten closer, if anything. Oh, there are certain ones that we don't want to be around, when you start talking, because -- let's get together. Well, I've got to tell you this story about critics, because you would appreciate it and it's part of the history.
